strategy.summary: SGDOneClassSVM with tol!=None stops after about 6 epochs because the convergence check uses only the loss term without regularization (and without the intercept for one-class SVM). The PR changes the stopping criterion to the full objective including penalty and intercept, and accumulates L1 norm in WeightVector. Reproduce by running the developer's test_sgd_oneclass_convergence on the buggy commit 86906384af8f (expected to fail with n_iter_ <= 6) and on the fixed revision (expected to pass with n_iter_ > 6 for all nu values).

system_packages: gcc or clang with OpenMP support
pinned_because: numpy, scipy, Cython versions are era-inferred from the reporter's environment (numpy 1.21.6, scipy 1.7.3, Cython 3.0.11); the README minimum versions are documented constraints and are the only ones to respect as floors, so use a modern numpy/scipy compatible with the buggy commit's build rather than the reporter's exact pins
Python 3.7.3 is the reporter's environment only and is not a stated requirement of this revision; do not pin it

strategy.reproducing_test: test_sgd_oneclass_convergence in sklearn/linear_model/tests/test_sgd.py: for nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9] fits SGDOneClassSVM(nu=nu, max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3) on iris.data and asserts model.n_iter_ > 6
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 86906384af8f, test_sgd_oneclass_convergence FAILS because n_iter_ is at most 6 for at least one nu (premature stop from loss-only convergence check). On the fixed revision (the PR), the same test PASSES because n_iter_ > 6 for all nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Fit SGDOneClassSVM(nu, max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3) on iris.data and read n_iter_; a value of 6 or less on the buggy revision indicates the premature stop

input_output_examples.input: SGDOneClassSVM with default stopping criteria on a higher-dimensional dataset (e.g. 10k samples, 10 or 1000 features)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Training stops after about 6 epochs (Avg. loss reported near 0.0 and then increasing)
input_output_examples.expected_output: Training continues until the objective converges (not stopped after 6 epochs)

risks: The regression test uses iris (4 features, 150 samples); the issue states the premature stop does not manifest on low-dimensional toy data, so test_sgd_oneclass_convergence may not fail on the buggy revision even though it is the developer's test; if it passes on buggy, the transition is not observed and this must be reported rather than forced.

The premature stop depends on the stopping tolerance rule (initial epoch plus 5 non-improving epochs), so results are sensitive to shuffling and random_state; the test does not set random_state, so the buggy run may vary.

Do not use tol=None as a substitute for the default-tolerance path; the second test test_sgd_oneclass_vs_linear_oneclass uses tol=None and does not exercise the bug; it also needs liblinear OneClassSVM and may be slow.
The second diff hunk in sklearn/tests/test_multioutput.py changes tol to None for SGDClassifier; that is a test-side workaround and should not be used as the reproducing test.
Dtype and precision of the bug run are not stated; the default float64 path is assumed.
BLAS/LAPACK backend is not stated in the evidence; the bug is in the sgd Cython loop and should not depend on BLAS, but this is not confirmed.
The reporter's Python 3.7.3 and numpy 1.21.6 are era-specific; running on a modern Python may require a build compatible with the current Cython, which is not in the evidence.
The changelog says output of SGD models can change for tol != None, so other SGD tests with default tol may shift on the fixed revision; this is not a regression for the transition but may be noisy.
No platform-specific behaviour (architecture or sanitiser) is stated; the transition is assumed to reproduce on a standard Linux x86_64 build with OpenMP.

oracle.reference_source: n_iter_ integer comparison in test_sgd_oneclass_convergence (asserts n_iter_ > 6); test_sgd_oneclass_vs_linear_oneclass uses assert_allclose and correlation thresholds but is not the transition test
oracle.why: The assertion is an integer epoch count threshold, so it is exact rather than tolerance-based

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy commit the loss-only convergence check stops training after about 6 epochs, so model.n_iter_ is at most 6 for at least one nu and the assertion n_iter_ > 6 fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the full objective (regularization and intercept) used for convergence, training continues beyond 6 epochs, so n_iter_ > 6 holds for nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9] and the test passes.
